issues.legal_issue: An emergency attachment of disputed property does not terminate the Magistrate’s jurisdiction to continue the possession inquiry.
material_facts: A dispute concerning a house was reported as likely to cause a breach of the peace.
The Magistrate made a preliminary order and attached the disputed property the following day, considering the case to be one of emergency.
After the attachment, the Magistrate proposed to continue the possession inquiry, but an objection was raised that he lacked jurisdiction to do so.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate’s jurisdiction did not end when the property was attached on the ground of emergency, and he was required to continue the inquiry. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 145 and 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, must be read together as a scheme for resolving disputes likely to cause a breach of the peace. Under Sections 145(4) and 145(6), the Magistrate must inquire into possession and make the appropriate consequential order; Section 145(5) permits the proceeding to stop when the likelihood of a breach of the peace has ceased. Section 146(1) permits attachment in an emergency after the preliminary order but does not expressly or impliedly end the Magistrate’s jurisdiction. Reading the sections contextually, the proceeding must run its course unless it is stopped under Section 145(5). The Court approved the reasoning in Kshetra Mohan Sarkar v. Puran Chandra Mandal and held that Chandu Naik v. Sitaram B. Naik did not decide this issue. The history of the 1955 amendments and the later return to the earlier scheme supported this construction.

rule.if: breach_of_peace_possession_proceeding and preliminary_order_issued and property_attached_for_emergency and inquiry_incomplete

predicates.breach_of_peace_possession_proceeding: A Magistrate initiated a proceeding concerning a possession dispute because it was likely to cause a breach of the peace.
predicates.preliminary_order_issued: The Magistrate issued a preliminary order calling on the parties to present their claims about actual possession.
predicates.property_attached_for_emergency: The Magistrate attached the disputed property because the case was considered an emergency.
predicates.inquiry_incomplete: The Magistrate had not completed the inquiry into which party was in possession when the property was attached.
predicates.magistrate_must_continue_possession_inqu: The Magistrate continues the possession inquiry after an emergency attachment.

issues.definition: When a Magistrate has issued a preliminary order in a breach-of-peace possession proceeding and has attached the property for emergency before completing the inquiry, the Magistrate must continue the possession inquiry.
